name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,240

clue.text: Baby elephant mostly quiet female

blocks.note: CALM, a word for quiet, without its last letter
the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A description of a young elephant that keeps quiet and happens to be a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one long description of the animal, but only the first two words define it; the rest is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The young of an elephant, like the young of a cow or whale, is called by this name.

clue.text: Disciple and saint in a bar

blocks.note: A plus POLE, a bar or rod
the usual abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A follower of Christ and a saint having a drink together in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it is a rod, a POLE; the saint slips inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the twelve followers chosen by Jesus is called an apostle, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Runs into whimsical American goddess

blocks.note: fey means otherworldly or whimsical
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
A is a common abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into an eccentric goddess from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs into' looks like a chance meeting; it is R going inside FEY, with A for American tacked on after.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse goddess of love and fertility, one of the chief deities in Scandinavian myth.

clue.text: Gateau served after meat in hunks

definitions.note: plural noun; the answer is a mass noun for muscular men collectively

blocks.note: beef is a common meat
a gateau is a rich cake

explanation.surface: A dessert of cake brought out after a meat course of thick chunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunks' reads as lumps of meat, but it means attractive muscular men.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefcake is slang for brawny, good-looking men displayed for admiration, which is what hunks are.

clue.text: Joe Root’s cricket club?

blocks.note: surface reading: the cricket club, the team or organisation, that the England batsman plays for
setter's reading: the club, the wooden implement, a cricketer swings to hit the ball

explanation.walkthrough: Joe Root is an England cricket captain and batsman; 'club' switches from a sports organisation to the wooden thing he hits with.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bat is a flat wooden implement used for striking, so it can be loosely called a club.

clue.text: De la Mare’s wild, tragic heroine

indicators.note: wild letters run out of control, so the poet's name with its possessive is jumbled

blocks.note: the poet Walter de la Mare's name with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A tragic, untamed heroine from one of Walter de la Mare's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter de la Mare was an English poet, so the clue suggests one of his characters; the heroine actually comes from Hugo's The Hunchback of Notre-Dame.
explanation.definitionFit: Esmeralda is the doomed gypsy girl in Victor Hugo's novel, hanged at its end: a classic tragic heroine.

clue.text: Sauce from copper with famous daughter

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a star is a famous person
the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A policeman's celebrated daughter is the source of some cheeky remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman and 'sauce' cheek; both are misdirection. Here 'famous' stands for a noun, a STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Custard is a sweet sauce poured over puddings in Britain, made from milk, eggs and sugar.

clue.text: Canoe going in either direction

blocks.note: a light boat paddled by one person
a word that reads the same forwards and backwards

explanation.surface: A boat that can be paddled forwards or backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half sounds like it describes how the boat moves; it describes the spelling of its name.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a narrow covered canoe of Inuit origin, and its letters read identically in both directions.

clue.text: Second Greek character backed Labour group

blocks.note: a second is a moment
mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A second Greek figure has thrown their support behind a Labour Party faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backed' reads as political support, but it reverses the letter. Momentum is a left-wing campaigning group within the UK Labour Party, formed in 2015 to back Jeremy Corbyn.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the name of an organised grassroots faction attached to Britain's Labour Party.

clue.text: Hellish river flows no more from mouth?

indicators.note: what comes from the mouth is spoken

blocks.note: something that sticks is stuck fast and no longer flows

explanation.surface: A river of the underworld has stopped running from its estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouth' looks like a river mouth, which fits the surface; it is the speaker's mouth, signalling a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Styx is the river of the underworld, Hades, across which the dead are ferried.

clue.text: Some returned from enchanted mountain

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: the middle letters of this word

explanation.surface: Some travellers have come back from a magical mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Enchanted mountain' looks like one phrase; 'enchanted' is only the word the letters sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, Europe's tallest active volcanic peak.

clue.text: Loudly criticises army accommodation

definitions.note: noun; the other definition is a verb

blocks.note: to jeer and heckle a performer or player
buildings where soldiers are housed

explanation.surface: Someone complains noisily about the quarters soldiers live in.
explanation.walkthrough: To barrack, in British and Australian usage, is to heckle or jeer at someone, often from the stands at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Barrack as a verb means to jeer; as a noun, barracks are the buildings housing troops.

clue.text: Bright idea: view a barn that’s renovated

indicators.note: a renovated building is rebuilt, so the letters of those three words are rebuilt too

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone has a clever plan: go and see a barn conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon makes the rest look like the content of the idea; it is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A brainwave is a sudden clever inspiration, the same thing as a bright idea.

clue.text: Roman stoic disrupted seance

indicators.note: a disrupted meeting is thrown into disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A calm Roman philosopher interrupts a meeting to contact the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'seance' are the answer's, and the answer is someone a seance might try to summon.
explanation.definitionFit: Seneca the Younger was a first-century Roman philosopher and leading writer of Stoic doctrine.

clue.text: Feeling close to marriage proposal

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end

blocks.note: the final letter of this word
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: Someone feels they are on the verge of popping the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near; it means the end of the word. 'Proposal' is not an offer of marriage but a motion for debate.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling such as joy, fear or anger, so they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Defect in hose that fireman uses

blocks.note: a run in stockings or tights
equipment carried on a fire engine for climbing

explanation.surface: A firefighter's hose has a flaw in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' means stockings here, not the fire hose; in British English a run in tights is called a ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is both a vertical run of broken threads in hosiery and the climbing frame firefighters use.

clue.text: First woman leading others in highest peak

blocks.note: in Genesis Eve is the first woman
the rest are the others

explanation.surface: The first woman leads a climbing party up the world's tallest mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the first woman to climb it; 'First woman' is simply the biblical EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Everest in the Himalayas is the tallest mountain on Earth above sea level.

clue.text: Minoan is astir: one possible cause

definitions.note: noun phrase: a cause of being astir, awake and moving at night

indicators.note: things astir are in motion, so the letters of the two words move around

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: An ancient Cretan is up and about at night, and the clue offers a reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Astir' works twice: it shuffles the letters, and being up and about at night is what the definition is a cause of.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleeplessness would explain why someone is awake and moving about at night, so it is a plausible cause.

clue.text: Relative close to collapse in French city

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end

blocks.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A family member is on the verge of collapsing while in a French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to collapse' reads as near breaking down; it means the last letter of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a kinswoman, the daughter of one's brother or sister, so a family relation.

clue.text: Ecstasy wrapped in cannabis for bard

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A writer takes a drug rolled up in a joint for inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Both drugs are slang abbreviations: E for ecstasy, POT for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Bard is a literary word for a poet, used especially of Shakespeare.

clue.text: One in plan to do the Wright thing?

definitions.note: stands for 'one to do the Wright thing', a noun, with 'One' shared with the wordplay

blocks.note: a plot is a plan or scheme
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone involved in a scheme to do what is morally correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Wright thing' puns on 'the right thing': the Wright brothers made the first powered flight, so the thing they did was fly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flies an aircraft, which is what Orville and Wilbur Wright famously first did in 1903.

clue.text: Shop in Indian metropolis did you say?

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to spoken words, so the city's name is heard not spelt

blocks.note: Delhi is India's capital region and a huge city

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a shop is located in a big Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Delhi and the shortened delicatessen are pronounced the same, the silent H making no difference.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Pains restricting poorly Greek hero

blocks.note: aches are pains
poorly means unwell

explanation.surface: Aches are holding back an ailing Greek warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' reads as an adverb describing how the pains restrict; it is an adjective meaning sick. Apt, since this hero was famously undone by a heel wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the great warrior of Homer's Iliad, the foremost Greek fighter at Troy.

clue.text: That woman seen in Chertsey

indicators.note: the answer can be seen sitting inside the town's name

blocks.note: letters two to four of this word

explanation.surface: A woman has been spotted in the Surrey town of Chertsey.
explanation.walkthrough: Chertsey is a small town in Surrey, England; only its spelling matters here.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun used to refer to a woman already mentioned, the object form of 'she'.

clue.text: Arctic animals check two rivers

blocks.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
DEE, a river in Britain, plus R, the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Polar creatures inspect a couple of waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Scotland (and another in Wales and England), a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Reindeer are antlered deer native to the tundra of the far north; the word serves as its own plural.

clue.text: Farewell from Indian steel producer

blocks.note: an informal British way of saying goodbye
the name of a major Indian industrial group with a large steel business

explanation.surface: A goodbye message from an Indian steelworks.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta-ta is a chirpy British goodbye; Tata is the Indian conglomerate whose steel arm owns plants worldwide.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is colloquial for goodbye, and Tata Steel is one of India's largest steel companies.
